title.value: Modeling electronic health record data using an end‐to‐end knowledge‐graph‐informed topic model
title.justification: The paper focuses on using a knowledge-graph-informed topic model for electronic health record data, as evident from the title, indicating the central use of a modeling approach for health records.
title.quote:
Modeling electronic health
record data using an end‐to‐end
knowledge‐graph‐informed topic
model

extractions.description: The paper presents a novel machine learning model named Graph ATtention-Embedded Topic Model (GAT-ETM) for extracting meaningful clinical knowledge from electronic health record (EHR) data. The model leverages a knowledge graph to inform embeddings used in topic modeling, aimed at improving patient stratification and drug recommendations based on EHR data analysis.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The focus is primarily on advancing data modeling for electronic health records rather than addressing specific ecological or climate-related sustainability goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We present Graph ATtention-Embedded Topic Model (GAT-ETM), an end-to-end taxonomy-knowledge-graph-based multimodal embedded topic model. GAT-ETM distills latent disease topics from EHR data by learning the embedding from a constructed medical knowledge graph.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper does not align directly with Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. Instead, it focuses on improving methods for analyzing electronic health records.
primary_category.quote:
The rapid growth of electronic health record (EHR) datasets opens up promising opportunities to
understand human diseases in a systematic way.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address any secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote:
GAT-ETM demonstrated superior performance
over the alternative methods on all tasks. Moreover, GAT-ETM learned clinically meaningful
graph-informed embedding of the EHR codes and discovered interpretable and accurate patient
representations for patient stratification and drug recommendations.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no mention of any direct sub-category of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development addressed by the paper.
primary_sub_category.quote:
We applied GAT-ETM to a large-scale EHR
dataset consisting of over 1 million patients.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No sub-category relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is addressed in the paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: GAT-ETM uses a graph attention network (GAT) to compute the embeddings of EHR codes from a taxonomy graph of the relations between and within the disease-code and drug-code modalities.

applications.justification: The applications discussed pertain to electronic health data analysis rather than climate or ecological applications.
applications.quote: GAT-ETM demonstrated high-quality topic inference and accurate drug imputation.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on innovative computational methods for analyzing electronic health records, which falls under the domain of Health Informatics.
new_primary_category.quote:
The rapid growth in volume and diversity of electronic health records (EHR) has enabled health informatics
research to refine disease phenotypes and discover novel disease comorbidities.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper concentrates on modeling electronic health record data using knowledge graphs, a technique within medical data analysis rather than sustainable development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We present a neural topic model called Graph-ATtention Embedded Topic Model (GAT-ETM).
